clips.title: The story
paras: Silvervein the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival atop the hills overlooking Thelsamar in Loch Modan. Travelers pay their respects to him to honor the ancient ties among Azeroth's elder peoples. In return for acknowledging his presence and heritage, he bestows his ancestral blessing.

Perched on the rolling ridges above Thelsamar, Elder Silvervein stands as a quiet guardian and reminder of antiquity. As a figure honored during the Lunar Festival, he represents the enduring memories of bygone eras. Even as the surrounding lands of Loch Modan grapple with trogg invasions and local disputes, Silvervein watches peacefully from his overlook.

The presence of spirits like Silvervein serves to bridge the divide between modern folk and ancient lineages. When adventurers seek him out, he expresses gratitude that travelers still pay homage to the olden races of Azeroth. His greeting carries the warmth of ancestral appreciation, offering a commemorative token to those who honor him.
